system.summary: Union military-telegraph route cipher: words written six to a row under a heading row, taken off up column 5, down 1, up 4, down 2, up 6, down 3; a commencement word gives the number of rows; local code words for places, names and military terms.

prior_solution.where: Decipherments of the time in the same collection: GLC02414.114 (grid of .341), .137 (clear copy of .229), .138 (clear copy of .344), and the grid on .185. None found for .339. None of the telegrams is printed in the Official Records, Series I, vol. 27, part 3.

conditions.human_role: Andrew Beling set the research direction and the posting restraint and opened the library subscription in his browser; AI agents transcribed, recovered the route and code words, froze the keys, ran both tests and packaged the folder. No human reading check.
tools: route undo and held-out scorer (freeze/round2, verify.py)
Huntington Digital Library IIIF images of Cipher Book No. 2

solution.what: Gilder Lehrman item pages blocked to curl (Cloudflare); the four telegrams and their siblings read in the Adam Matthew edition through a library subscription.
Cipher telegrams .341, .229, .339, .344 transcribed (two passes for three of them) and the decipherment grid .114.
Route recovered by matching .341 with its decipherment grid .114: up 5, down 1, up 4, down 2, up 6, down 3; 34 of 36 positions agree, 2 hidden under a repair patch; six code words.

Round 1 test written before scoring: share of word pairs attested in the Eckert telegram ledgers against 200 random routes. All four telegrams failed, the crib included: the measure cannot separate routes.
Check devised after the failure, labelled as such: random routes putting the heading words in row 1 as the frozen route does: 1 to 4 of 10,000.
Inventory of GLC02414 by catalogue searches and neighbours: clear copies .137 and .138 found for .229 and .344, the self-contained pair .185, and ten decipherment grids whose ciphers were not found.
Code words valued from .229/.137, .344/.138 and the corrections in .110; commencement words shown to give the row count (Florida 6, Dacotah 7, Wilderness 9, Ocean 10, Turkey 2).

Round 2 held-out test written before scoring: frozen key_v2 predicted the .185 decipherment grid from its cipher: 60 of 66 cells; 200 random routes median 1, maximum 40. The agent had glanced at the .185 sheet before writing the protocol (disclosed).

.339 read in part with the frozen key plus plated and nile from .185: 35 of 42 cells, one inferred (Camp Piatt); 7 code words unvalued. Arrangement with the darker-ink '&' counted chosen at packaging.
Route and commencement words compared with Cipher Books No. 1, 2 and 9 (Huntington mssEC 43, 47, 67; Plum 1882 appendix): no match; No. 12 not available.
Unvalued .339 code words tried against Official Records I/27/3 (Scammon's railroad expedition, Toland's brigade of 8 July): guesses only, no value assigned.

Independent check by a second AI agent of the project: route derived from the .341 and .114 images before it opened the folder; same route and code-word values; 70 of 70 checkable cells on .229, 54 of 54 on .344, 60 of 66 on .185 reproduced. Its corrections applied: heading row, commencement words stated as an untested observation, sources of rye and amazon, single occurrences marked, 'head' for 'had', Venus/Agnes and Italy/truly uncertain and outside the count (14 code words valued), .339 alternative readings and counts with and without later additions.

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: The route and the code words were recovered by matching the cipher telegrams with decipherments of the time kept as separate items in the same collection (.114, .137, .138); the frozen key then predicted a held-out decipherment (.185, 60 of 66 cells) and was applied to .339, which has none.
outcome.fraction_read_source: verify.py grids, unit grid cells (cipher words less commencement words): 270 cells over five telegrams (.341 36, .229 72, .344 54, .185 66, .339 42); 7 holes, all in .339. In .339 alone 35 of 42 (0.833), one inferred and three later additions in other ink or hand (32 of 42 without them).

gaps.item: .339: code words Virginia, Missouri, gaol, bent, amore, away and the first nile without a value
gaps.detail: No second message with these words and no decipherment of the time found; book not identified.

gaps.item: .339: placement of the darker-ink '&' and the margin 'when not' chosen by sense
gaps.detail: Whose hand added them, and when, cannot be settled from the image.

gaps.item: the cipher book behind the route, commencement words and code words
gaps.detail: Books 1, 2 and 9 do not fit; No. 10 and No. 12 not seen.

gaps.item: .341: two words under the paper repair patch

validation.notes: Route transposition of whole words with a code layer: the character-level test has no token alignment to score. The key was instead tested on a held-out decipherment written before scoring (freeze/round2: 60 of 66 cells; 200 random routes, maximum 40).

credits.note: Andrew Beling, with AI agents: transcriptions, route and code words recovered from the 1863 pairs, the held-out test on .185 (60 of 66), and the partial reading of .339.
Scammon's headquarters, 1863: decipherment grid .114 of .341, clear copies .137 of .229 and .138 of .344; the decipherer of .185 on the same sheet.
The same decipherments supplied the route and the code-word values (and .110 the values of cedar and cotton).

texts.label: GLC02414.341, White to Scammon, Fayette, 2 July 1863
texts.summary: A soldier's wife from the head of Paint Creek reports that the 45th and 22nd Virginia were to leave Lewisburg.
texts.note: Two grid words under the repair patch supplied from .114. Words 2 (Venus/Agnes) and 14 (Italy/truly) are uncertain readings; the cells read 'yours' and 'Truly' in .114 either way.

reading_review.by: the packaging AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5), one of the contributor's own agents, not a human review
reading_review.note: Read the grid and the sentence against .114; agrees word for word apart from spelling variants.

texts.label: GLC02414.229, White to Scammon, Fayette, 2 July 1863
texts.summary: Confederates fortifying at the ford of Piney, 45th Virginia at Pack's Ferry, 22nd moving to Raleigh; talk of an attack with six thousand to take Fayette, which White doubts.

reading_review.by: the packaging AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5), one of the contributor's own agents, not a human review
reading_review.note: Read against the clear copy .137; all 72 cells agree once telegraph slips are allowed.

texts.label: GLC02414.344, White to Scammon, Fayette, 3 July 1863, 9.35 p.m.
texts.summary: Enemy cavalry seen near the outpost; White sends his cavalry to drive the enemy pickets into Raleigh at two in the morning.

reading_review.by: the packaging AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5), one of the contributor's own agents, not a human review
reading_review.note: Read against the clear copy .138; all 54 cells agree once telegraph slips are allowed.

texts.label: GLC02414.185, Toland to [Scammon], 1863 (held-out pair)
texts.summary: Toland finds no powder or fuse in the army wagon, has started at three in the morning, and asks where the enemy is going.
texts.note: The decryption file is the frozen-key prediction (60 of 66 cells); the reading uses the grid of the time.

reading_review.by: the packaging AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5), one of the contributor's own agents, not a human review
reading_review.note: Compared the prediction cell by cell with the grid of the time; six misses, all listed in NOTES.

texts.label: GLC02414.339, Camp Piatt to 'Operator', 1 July 1863, signed by code as Toland
texts.summary: Toland gives Scammon 'our united opinion' and asks, if the movement is important, when it shall start, and whether it will interfere with a proposed operation; written a fortnight before his raid toward Wytheville.
texts.note: 7 holes; Camp Piatt inferred from the heading slot; 3 of the 35 cells read are later additions (&, when, not): 32 of 42 (0.762) without them; 37 of 42 under a second reader's 'gave' and 'will'. Arrangement with the '&' chosen by sense; a second reader reached the same.

reading_review.by: the packaging AI agent (Claude Opus 5.5), one of the contributor's own agents, not a human review
reading_review.note: Read the grid as sentences in both arrangements; rows 3-7 read in arrangement B with holes marked; no decipherment of the time to compare.

outcome.notes: No image is included (licensed edition). .229, .341 and .344 were read in 1863; the key was built from them, so their readings are not tests. 14 code words valued in the frozen key (Venus/Agnes and Italy/truly uncertain, not counted); 7 of them rest on one occurrence. A second AI agent of the project checked the work independently (not a human check).
